quality_target: Kinnaird-class architectural identity in a modular, real-time City Prompt GLB
purpose: Preserve the construction knowledge learned during the high-fidelity LEGO pilots and make it executable for catalogue-scale batches.

non_negotiable_principles.rule: Every production variant must pass reference sufficiency, representation selection, clay massing, roof and void construction, medium detail, retopology, manual UV audit, material bake, export parity and named architect review in order. Missing evidence or a failed stage is a hard stop, never a warning.

Compare the exact archetype against street/front, front-corner, rear-corner, high-oblique or roof, close-facade and context views. Require at least 85/100 and no hard-stop architectural error for every building; a batch average cannot approve an individual rejection.

For irregular curtain walls and highly ornamental curved facades, let an image-locked semantic surface carry fine identity while separate physical glazing, structure, balconies, rails, roofs, returns and executable voids carry transmission, depth, silhouette and shadow. Exclude generic kits that duplicate or contradict the exact variant.

A continuous image-locked elevation owns its visible windows and fine frames until an opening-accurate semantic glass mask is approved in the same metres-to-UV registration frame. Physical optical overlays may add transmission and recess only inside that mask; generic pane schedules that cover or duplicate photographed openings are a release-blocking ownership error.

Before generating a landmark sticker, approve a source-traced roof and silhouette proxy plus an all-elevation occupancy map. Blank visible sides or rears, generic roof boxes, duplicated physical/sticker gables and unregistered porches or balconies are pre-render hard stops. Camera-match final review views; source-to-GLB parity measures export fidelity, not archetype likeness.

A fixed Sticker Method landmark must declare one registered owner for every exposed exterior wall, chamfer, courtyard wall and roof weathering field. Crop isolation backgrounds before registration, align entrance-block outer faces to the facade plane, and replace only roof albedo so the approved PBR normal and roughness survive. Blank fields, pale crop borders and independently scaled roof stickers are pre-release failures.

Semantic textures whose alpha controls facade identity must use a lossless glTF-compatible image path and pass a camera-locked transparent source-versus-reimport comparison. Lossy packing of alpha-bearing textures is an export-parity failure even when geometry validates.

A building whose identity depends on one registered metres-to-UV frame is a fixed select-and-place landmark. Translation and rotation are allowed; polygon fitting, floor-count changes and non-uniform scaling are forbidden. Arbitrary LEGO capacity changes require a different repeatable-bay representation.

Alpha-isolated feature stickers must retain their unique material node trees after mesh joining. Consolidating them into the opaque elevation material discards the mask and exposes rectangular crop edges; this is a pre-release hard stop.

A non-rectangular public opening must use one versioned inner negative-space contour extracted from the exact registered source or an approved binary mask. That contour cuts every crossing sticker and generates the inset jamb/soffit section; inferred style curves, decorative-frame traces and independently tuned geometry are release-blocking mismatches.

Before expanding a catalogue campaign to one hundred, complete and visually classify ten exact variants. A failed semantic, proportion, roof, side/rear or export-parity gate blocks scale-up; never lower a threshold or average away a rejected pilot.

Count storeys and classify reference opening shapes before facade generation. Reject a facade atlas that invents arches, changes the bay hierarchy or changes the visible floor count even when its technical texture checks pass.

Use lightweight registered mask-only glazing for large repeated modern curtain walls and reserve complete returns, frames and occupied cavities for identity-bearing heritage openings, entrances and arcades. One feature has one owner; do not duplicate atlas construction as a floating geometry cage.

Plan every exact variant explicitly, complete one representative per parent before sibling expansion, cap each production batch at five buildings, render serially and require a human exact-reference checkpoint after every batch. Machine success cannot approve catalogue release.

Catalogue rendering defaults to zero paid facade-image calls. Estimate missing assets in planning, but reject paid calls in the batch runner and require a separate explicitly authorized asset-generation step.
Use every compatible archetype view to infer massing, corners, roof, entrances and side elevations; never optimize only for the card image.

Reference images are authoritative. Admit metadata field by field only when it is image-confirmed and bound to a specific construction purpose; ignore conflicting or generic parent prose, and allow metadata to be disabled entirely.

Before Blender, convert exact street, oblique and roof images into a bounded feature schedule: dimensions, storey and opening counts, opening positions, ridge axes, roof intersections, material zones and depth-bearing voids. Every measurement names the graph node, assembly or void it drives, and production preflight fails when required topology is missing.

A reference-visible door, shop bay or market stall needs more than a void and dark back plane. Preserve the real section, then add a bounded identity kit at the opening: door leaf panels and fanlight, or counters, crates, goods, shelving and warm task lights. Fine occupation may repeat inside approved bays but cannot replace the fixed opening geometry.
Silhouette-changing and shadow-casting features are geometry. A facade photograph must not be asked to hide generic massing.
Keep corner, entrance, podium, crown and roof assemblies fixed. Repeat or stretch only authored middle bays.
Close-range facades use shadow-neutral albedo plus normal, roughness, AO/depth and emissive channels. City lighting remains the lighting authority.

A baked surface source must match the visible construction role and pattern, not merely its broad material family or colour. Treat pantile, wall brick, ashlar, rusticated stone, standing seam and built-up roof membrane as distinct reviewed source roles and declare the role for every required baked material.

Use recessed panes, frame depth, registered physical mullions/transoms, interior backplates and occupied warm interiors. Use physical transmission near and baked facade glass far; an audited atlas may supply fine sash colour but not all close-range construction depth.

Dormers, oriels, lanterns and gable windows use the same two-layer contract as facade openings: a physically shaded pane in front of a recessed occupied room card. A single opaque warm pane cannot provide reflections, parallax and interior depth at once.

Semantic glazing masks must follow the actual glass field: pointed and segmental arches, roundels and tracery groups may not be approximated by rectangular bounding boxes. The mask controls both the facade cut-out and the physical pane, so its silhouette is construction geometry at hero range.

Every near-range glazing assembly owns an unobstructed service cavity from exterior skin to occupied backplate. Structural massing cores must be inset far enough that panes and room cards never intersect or disappear behind the core.

Author front, left, right and rear elevations for every asset, including courtyard walls. Material courses, cornices, balconies, window returns and roof logic continue around exposed sides and corners; secondary elevations remain stylistically related but use a believable different opening and service hierarchy. Detail may be occluded only when site geometry confirms a true party wall.
Roofs, dormers, canopies, columns and other fixed assemblies inherit the archetype's material palette, edge profiles and construction logic; no attachment may introduce a separate visual language.

Every large visible fixed assembly names an archetype material slot and resolves to an available texture family at preflight and render time. Turrets, gables, crenellations and roof forms may not fall back to an untextured colour when the catalogue metadata or references identify granite, slate, copper, tile or another construction material.

At hero range, a large pitched roof must show its actual covering and edge system: overlapping courses or seams, ridge and valley caps, verge/fascia thickness, drainage, and any archetype-specific ballast or snow retention. A smooth prism supplies massing only, not a finished roof.
A family is not production-ready until it works at recommended small and large sizes and on every declared footprint profile.

Compare archetype and model at block, building and facade scales using a street/front view, front-corner oblique, rear-corner oblique, high oblique/aerial, close facade and context view. No family is production-ready from one hero angle.

A release contract declares at least street-identity and roof-plan roles, scores each camera independently and fails when any required role fails. A mean score may summarize but never override a failed view.

A signature arch, portal, undercroft or carved entrance is authored as a depth-bearing section with outer shell, inner reveal and inhabited back plane. Flat facade imagery or trim cannot carry a public void.

A declared gate passage, arcade or undercroft must name its target mass, minimum depth, opening shape and every facade skin that must clear it. The renderer must construct or subtract that volume; recording a void beside a solid node is not an implementation.

A wave, barrel or tensile landmark roof is a closed sampled assembly with outer skin, soffit and sealed perimeter. Plan pinch, sectional crests and surface-following panel seams remain physical geometry and must read in both street and roof-plan evidence.

A machine-scored roof or plan audit hides every presentation mesh except the building. Ground, roads, trees, cars and neighbouring masses may appear in human context views but may not enter the segmentation image.
Natatoria, hangars and civic halls may legitimately encode one 8-18 m internal level. Preserve that catalogue height through compilation and let an image-locked landmark graph own the final section.

Plazas, aprons, streets and public-realm surfaces visible in reference images belong to placement context unless the catalogue footprint explicitly includes them. Keep the exported building inside its declared structural envelope.

Generate a photoreal City Prompt render from each authoritative live camera and treat it as a construction goal post. The prompt must preserve the exact footprint, massing, height, roofline, silhouette, window rhythm and camera; it may improve materials, lighting and entourage but must not redesign the building. Compare the unchanged live 3D camera back to that image after every keeper iteration.
A materially or geometrically distinct catalogue variant owns its signature profile, reference provenance, physical atlas span and fixed massing assemblies; never inherit the parent family blindly.

A selected variant may inherit reusable geometry but never a parent or sibling photographic facade sheet. Resolve and audit the exact variant reference before facade generation, and keep roof, tower and gable imagery out of repeatable rectangular wall crops.

The selected catalogue variant must rewrite generationStyleInput, image provenance and generation identifier before family export. Validate the resolved UI id and source thumbnail so sibling variants can never silently compile as variant_0.

Weathered timber grain, murals, flower boxes and masonry joints are not glazing evidence. For irregular vernacular elevations, use an audited opening schedule before creating physical panes or frames; automatic masks remain texture-only evidence until reviewed.
Every production family declares whether identity is carried by an archetype-specific massing graph or by a tightly authored semantic stack. Unclassified generic stacks cannot enter paid generation.
Variant provenance, three compatible reference roles, the fixed/repeatable decomposition and canonical graph dimensions must pass a grammar-only preflight before any image API or Blender work.

Structural validation never implies archetype likeness. A generated family remains review-only until a named reviewer approves block, building, facade and orbit/context comparisons against the authoritative reference set.

Use a camera-locked OpenCV silhouette, roofline and aspect-ratio contract to catch gross drift, but never treat its pass as likeness approval. Pair it with explicit landmark hierarchy and roof-plan checks because an incorrect solid box can share the correct outer boundary.

Courtyards, quadrangles, light wells and gate passages visible in an authoritative roof or aerial reference are fixed plan geometry. They may not survive only as metadata inside an otherwise solid massing core.

Curved and faceted corners use the same floor-accurate podium, middle and crown band stack as orthogonal elevations; never stretch one floor or one complete elevation over a multi-storey corner surface.

Balconies, cornices, rails and other identity-defining projections must follow the authored corner curve. Straight tangent fragments may approximate surface infill, but they may not leave silhouette datums broken at the corner.

Before reference imagery becomes PBR input, separate material appearance from view lighting and confidence-mask uncertain regions. Luminance-derived roughness, normal or depth maps are fallback-only because baked shadows and highlights make the asset fight runtime lighting.

Each fixed skyscraper setback tier repeats the audited ordinary floor band vertically with a shared bay phase. Setback caps, entrances and crowns remain fixed and may not be produced by stretching one full-height image.

Measure the user's drawn geographic polygon for every assembly. Catalogue dimensions guide suitability, but a native named tier should be authored when the real parcel would otherwise require excessive scaling.

Clip source tiles in world coordinates for a single replacement footprint so photogrammetry behind the proposal remains visible; projected stencil silhouettes are not acceptable in close orbit or render captures.

A complete category is a finite registry of exact variants. Every variant owns its reference roles, orthographic facade source, audited opening and band schedules, signature graph, native dimensions and fidelity contract; category labels never authorize sibling reuse.

Rectangular facade skins use body-only crops. Sky, isolation background, shaped gables, roof slopes and fixed end insertions stay out of repeatable elevation bands and are represented by fixed geometry or dedicated skins.

Do not place a generic curtain-wall cage over a reference-authored glass field. Add physical panes and frames only when their span, depth and cadence are registered to the atlas; otherwise retain the audited facade and model only the larger structural frame.

After silhouette, roof, void and projection geometry are approved, a high-quality image-locked surface may be split into thin semantic architectural stickers for wall fields, galleries, oriels, balcony faces and roof pieces. Every piece must preserve the same canonical metres-to-UV transform and shared window, column and floor-datum anchors. Seam bleed expands object-space and UV-space bounds by the identical physical distance; any drift blocks generation.

Infer ridge axis, valleys, cross-gables, hips, green-roof drainage and photovoltaic layout from compatible 60-degree and 90-degree references. Catalogue roof labels are hints, not sufficient construction evidence.

Each silhouette contract names the generated view whose projection best matches its authoritative reference. A single global hero camera may be used for presentation, but it must not force a false aspect or roofline comparison.

Decompose every image-locked landmark into fixed ceremonial/end modules, repeatable structural bays and explicit material fields. Repeat only inside declared spans; never stretch the entrance, corner, clock tower, roof termination or another identity-bearing module.

Approve large silhouette and section first, then medium shadow-bearing construction such as pilasters, cornices, ribs, purlins and side openings, then fine baked or instanced ornament. Fine detail cannot rescue wrong massing, and large geometry must not carry texture-scale noise.

Glass roof fields and opaque cladding occupy separate geometry with visible supporting structure and an unobstructed volume below. Never place transmissive glass over an opaque shell and call the result a glazed roof.

Keep sun, world, fill, camera and context outside the exported GLB, but make them a reproducible presentation contract. Compare Cycles, Eevee and runtime Three.js independently so renderer parity problems are not misdiagnosed as missing geometry or vice versa.

For a bounded pilot, preserve the approved silhouette, voids and physical material section before consolidating repeated meshes, baking non-silhouette ornament or reducing texture payloads. Optimization must satisfy explicit triangle, material and delivery-envelope gates without erasing archetype evidence.

Use metric UV scale and restrained location-specific albedo, roughness and normal variation, then bake the result into ordinary image maps that survive glTF export. Compare the same neutral camera from the Blender source and a re-imported GLB; a beauty render cannot substitute for export parity.

Treat surface finish, medium construction and archetype-specific sculptural ornament as separate approvals. Better stone and roof shaders may remove plastic flatness, but they cannot prove tower proportion, carved relief, balustrade cadence or silhouette fidelity.

When a material uses baked PBR maps, the actual albedo pixels are the delivered colour authority. A declared base colour does not repair an incompatible dark, pale or hue-shifted bake; compare the baked map itself with exact facade or roof evidence before rendering.

Assign each visible architectural feature one owning representation at each distance band. Do not independently encode the same loggia, mullion, frame or ornament in both an audited facade sheet and projecting geometry unless the layers have explicit non-overlapping responsibilities.

instructions: Reject or quarantine reference views that depict a different variant.
Record invariant cues shared by the views before writing geometry.
For one-view archetypes, lower confidence and require visual review.

always_model: entrance recess and canopy support logic
window recesses and stone returns at hero range
cornice profiles and wrapping balcony slabs
curve-native rails and supports wherever a fixed rounded corner carries the archetype identity
bevels on exposed masonry, metal and timber edges
signature elements that alter silhouette or cast identity-defining shadows
blend_rules: Never allow columns, pilasters or buttresses to cross window openings unless shown in the reference.
Every projection requires a believable attachment, return or support.
Use bevelled or profiled edges; avoid razor-sharp boxes on visible corners.
Place fixed corner geometry inside the module extent contract.
Weathering surfaces inherit the roof family; supports and fascias inherit facade masonry; frames and flashings inherit the building metal family.
Keep ceremonial entrances and landmark roof pavilions fixed in size while repeatable middle bays absorb footprint changes.
Reserve landmark bays before distributing repeatable dormers or windows so semantic assemblies never collide.
For wide landmark frontages preserve a fixed corner / secondary pavilion / centre pavilion / secondary pavilion / corner rhythm; only the bays between those anchors absorb width changes.
Continue every projected pavilion through the vertical LEGO stack and terminate it with a matching roof assembly; a facade projection without a skyline consequence reads as an applique.
Evaluate roof material inheritance from the City Prompt aerial camera as well as the hero view; horizontal roof surfaces hidden in a street render still dominate the Google Tiles scene.

Before export, compare exterior-skin, pane, room-card and structural-core planes on every facade axis; preserve a positive clearance behind the room card after all recess caps and coordinate transforms.

required_properties: separate podium, typical, alternate and crown bands
export-baked albedo, roughness and normal variation
semantic weathering limited to plausible material zones
facade_pbr.delivery: KTX2/UASTC for close range, smaller compressed LOD for city scale

glazing.near: physical transmission, shape-matched recessed pane, semantic opening returns, slim registered mullions/transoms, projecting sill and occupied interior backplate
glazing.far: baked facade glass with semantic mask
glazing.occupancy_rule: Default visible windows to subtle warm occupied interiors; avoid uniform dark-blue panes.

lod.hero_strategy: physical glazing, full PBR atlas and semantic relief
lod.city_strategy: compressed baked facade, preserved silhouette and simplified interiors

batch_workflow.automation: Collect archetype, variant, all reference images, dimensions and footprint metadata; assign a confidence score.
batch_workflow.human_review: Only missing or contradictory reference sets.

batch_workflow.automation: Group entries by massing graph, architectural signature kits, material zones, roof family and glass profile.
Compile grammar, inject signature, check reference roles and footprint ranges without image API calls.
Generate or reuse a rectified facade source, perform intrinsic/de-lighting decomposition with confidence masks where available, derive full PBR channels, semantic glass masks and LOD atlases.
batch_workflow.human_review: Only failed rectification, uncertain material regions, baked shadows, inconsistent floors or lost identity.

batch_workflow.automation: Build fixed semantic modules plus repeatable middle variants, wrap side elevations and export GLBs.
Validate origin, extents, stack, file integrity, quality-memory gates, shape matrix and LOD budgets.

Move the City Prompt camera through street/front, front-corner oblique, rear-corner oblique, high oblique/aerial and close-facade roles; generate camera-locked photoreal goal posts; compare the live model at the unchanged cameras plus a context view.
batch_workflow.human_review: Approve one representative per cluster, then spot-check confidence outliers.

batch_workflow.automation: Import only validation-pass and high-quality-ready manifests into City Prompt; retain provenance and memory version.

triangle_budget.policy: warn outside range; landmarks may exceed with explicit waiver

review_routing.pass: Eligible for automated City Prompt import after one cluster representative has visual approval.
review_routing.review: Continue the batch but add to the visual-review queue with failed gate reasons.
review_routing.fail: Do not import; retain logs and inputs for a resumable retry.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A model passes silhouette comparison but still has the wrong tower hierarchy or a missing courtyard
known_failure_patterns.cause: The image metric measures the normalized exterior boundary and roofline but cannot see internal plan voids or distinguish which landmark produced each skyline peak.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Keep the silhouette test as a regression gate, then audit named landmark positions, relative heights and the roof-plan occupancy mask against every compatible reference view before visual approval.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Boxy or cartoonish building
known_failure_patterns.cause: Generic rectangular massing with identity delegated to a flat image.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Add semantic massing, recesses, bevels, profiles and fixed signature assemblies.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Roof windows look pasted on
known_failure_patterns.cause: Dormer material, depth and roof attachment do not match the roof system.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Integrate dormer cheeks and caps into the roof material and add occupied recessed glazing.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Cartoon ground floor
known_failure_patterns.cause: Flat doors, oversized frames, uniform glass and unsupported awning slabs.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Model recessed shopfront bays, transoms, kickplates, stone piers, dark timber/bronze doors and supported canopies only.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Dead dark-blue windows
known_failure_patterns.cause: Tinted alpha-blended planes without interiors or reflections.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use physical transmission near and subtle warm occupied backplates; bake semantic glass far.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Front facade works but orbit view fails
known_failure_patterns.cause: Materials and architectural datums stop at the front edge.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Wrap materials, bands, returns and compatible detail around side elevations.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Detail collides with windows
known_failure_patterns.cause: Signature kits are placed on a generic spacing grid instead of the bay graph.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Derive every projection from semantic bay occupancy and test opening clearance.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Generated surface fights City Prompt lighting
known_failure_patterns.cause: Directional shadows and highlights are baked into albedo.
known_failure_patterns.correction: De-light albedo and keep lighting authority in the runtime environment.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: One rectangle looks good but user polygons fail
known_failure_patterns.cause: Corners and entrances were stretched with the middle facade.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use fixed semantic end conditions and test every declared footprint profile at small and large dimensions.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A showcase graph silently falls back to generic balcony modules
known_failure_patterns.cause: The authored reference dimensions or floor count do not match the pilot registry exactly.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Treat reference dimensions as an executable contract and preflight the selected width, depth and floors before rendering.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Physical curtain-wall grid looks like a second cage over the facade
known_failure_patterns.cause: Frame colour, bay count or datum does not match the rectified elevation.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Align physical mullions to the authored facade cadence, keep profiles shallow and use the archetype's metal finish rather than a universal black grid.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Landmark GLB has excessive materials despite using a small atlas set
known_failure_patterns.cause: Temporary per-elevation UV-bound shader clones survive into export.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Bake surface-specific bounds into vertex UVs, then remap clones to their canonical shared material before GLB export.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Generated source is beautiful but changes the archetype's storey count or massing
known_failure_patterns.cause: The image model optimized architectural plausibility without a strict elevation contract.
known_failure_patterns.correction: A/B providers only for failed sources, reject attractive but structurally unfaithful results, and preserve the accepted provider plus reference provenance in the cache.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Parallel 4K PBR derivation exhausts memory
known_failure_patterns.cause: Several full-resolution albedo, normal, roughness, AO and emissive arrays are resident simultaneously.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Limit PBR image derivation concurrency while allowing geometry compilation and lightweight validation to remain parallel.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Semantic window relief becomes oversized rectangles or a facade cage
known_failure_patterns.cause: A coarse or fallback glass mask was treated as precise opening geometry.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use mask-only physical glazing until semantic regions are opening-accurate; add construction-scale relief from known bay datums rather than outlining uncertain mask groups.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Gothic, Romanesque or segmental windows acquire dark rectangular patches in close City Prompt views
known_failure_patterns.cause: The semantic glass schedule stored only rectangular bounding boxes, so the near facade cut-out, physical glass plane and room-card reveal ignored the authored arch silhouette.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Rasterize an audited shape-aware mask from the same registered boxes (pointed_arch, segmental_arch, round or polygon), rebuild every PBR LOD from that mask, and compare the same grazing camera before acceptance.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Chamfered corner is a blank wedge between otherwise finished elevations
known_failure_patterns.cause: Cardinal facade skins stop where the diagonal corner condition begins.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Author oriented facade skins for every visible chamfer, keep a fixed entrance corner, and validate both street diagonals plus the aerial view.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Historic landmark has detailed fronts but blank projecting sides
known_failure_patterns.cause: Tower and pavilion modules received front elevations without return-face material assignments.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Treat every projection as a small building: wrap both return faces, continue the roof junction, and validate orbit views before acceptance.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: European balconies look like black boxes attached to the facade
known_failure_patterns.cause: Solid end panels and unsupported slabs were used as shortcuts for open iron construction.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use thin slabs, open end rails, regularly spaced pickets, small corbels and floor-datum alignment; never close an iron balcony with opaque end plates.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A high-quality facade becomes a flat hundred-metre wall when the user widens the parcel
known_failure_patterns.cause: The centre and corner identities were preserved but all intermediate frontage was treated as one repeat field.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use a bounded five-part landmark rhythm with fixed secondary quarter pavilions, then distribute only ordinary bays inside the four remaining intervals.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: The street view is coherent but the tiles aerial shows a giant unrelated dark lid
known_failure_patterns.cause: A generic flat lead or membrane deck closed a heritage mansard above the visible eaves.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Close the roof with the archetype material and form—such as a verdigris hipped cap—and validate the entire upper plane from an oblique aerial camera.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: One generated family is selected for visually incompatible variants of the same catalogue archetype
known_failure_patterns.cause: Broad aliases used a parent ID even though variant reference sets encode different massing and stylistic identities.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Persist reference provenance at variant level, give each materially distinct variant its own family, and never broaden aliases merely to satisfy a stale selection ID.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A landmark facade repeats miniature towers or entrances across a user-sized frontage
known_failure_patterns.cause: The complete rectified elevation was registered with the default repeatable-bay span instead of its audited real-world building span.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Audit and persist the physical atlas span before PBR derivation; reserve complete elevations for fixed massing and repeat only explicitly cropped middle bays.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A pale sky or blank background is printed onto the top of a Gothic or monumental volume
known_failure_patterns.cause: Negative space around towers in a complete orthographic elevation was treated as opaque rectangular facade material.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Reject the generic stack and split the target into fixed tower/crown skins plus background-free repeatable wing or nave bands.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Photoreal brick or glass is crossed by pale rails, dark cages or mismatched columns
known_failure_patterns.cause: A generic geometry kit duplicated coursing, fins or piers already authored in the render-locked atlas, or assigned the wrong semantic material.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Let the audited atlas own micro-detail; add only shadow-casting depth, map each kit to the target material language and suppress geometry absent from the reference.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A heritage cornice becomes a blank full-height storey
known_failure_patterns.cause: The fixed crown inherited the typical floor height instead of its measured architectural height.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Store a variant-level crown height and assemble it independently from repeatable floors.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Mansard dormers read as blue boxes while the facade windows feel occupied
known_failure_patterns.cause: Generic physical glass was used in a deep historic roof opening without a room backplate.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use recessed warm occupied interior cards for heritage dormers, with roof-matched cheeks, stone surrounds and lead or slate aprons.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: The generated model occupies only part of the drawn parcel
known_failure_patterns.cause: The assembly fell back to a catalogue suggested width and depth because footprint compatibility metadata was absent.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Always analyze the actual polygon, author a named native dimension tier when needed, and verify the selected plan's fit scale before placement.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Pale or empty wedges appear behind an otherwise correct model in Google Tiles
known_failure_patterns.cause: A projected stencil volume erased tile fragments that were behind the replacement in screen space but outside its geographic footprint.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use true world-coordinate clipping for the single replacement footprint and do not mount the projected stencil volume at the same time.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A deleted 3D model cannot be rebuilt on its surviving planning polygon
known_failure_patterns.cause: A stale community compile marker or historical building ID still classified the zone as placed.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Treat the primary live building link as authoritative; an unlinked zone is ready to place and recipe saves must never target stale secondary IDs.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Front signs, entrances or fire escapes repeat around side and rear elevations
known_failure_patterns.cause: The principal elevation atlas and semantic mask were reused on every face.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Generate a clean secondary-elevation bay with its own semantic mask and physical repeat span, preserve it through PBR/LOD derivation, and register side/rear relief to that band.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Accurate windows acquire heavy black picture-frame outlines at close range
known_failure_patterns.cause: A complete physical perimeter frame was added over sash already present in the audited facade atlas.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Do not duplicate the outer perimeter. Let the atlas own its fine colour/weathering, but register slim physical mullions and transoms at the recessed pane plane so grazing views still have parallax and contact shadow.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Masonry window returns look like applied trim instead of wall depth
known_failure_patterns.cause: Return boxes were centred on the opening boundary, leaving half their width visible on the wall face.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Inset non-heritage jambs, head and sill wholly inside the semantic opening. Validate from head-on and grazing cameras in Google Tiles.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A high-quality facade contains blank gray or white vertical panels after LEGO resizing
known_failure_patterns.cause: The rectified source retained isolation-background margins or a fixed end insertion inside the repeatable middle crop.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Crop the elevation and semantic mask together to the building silhouette, then remove fixed end insertions from the middle-band source and model those insertions as fixed geometry.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A roof reads as generic blue slab, Quonset huts or floating black sticks
known_failure_patterns.cause: A signature barrel or glazed lantern was approximated with generic primitives and unconstrained roof equipment.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Suppress generic roof clutter and author the target section: shallow elliptical closed shells for barrel vaults, slope-registered ribs and ridge for glazed lanterns, and real columns, beams, timber slats and planters for occupied terraces.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Adding physical sash makes the textured facade disappear in the close City Prompt LOD
known_failure_patterns.cause: The runtime treated any near-only material, including a glazing frame, as proof that a complete replacement near facade sheet existed and hid the baked wall.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Detect replacement near facades by the near-sheet material identity or facade-sheet metadata only. Near-only frames, glass and interiors must not hide the baked facade when the city-detail asset has no complete near sheet.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A generated elevation becomes blank walls, doubled storeys or sky-colored crown panels in the modular model
known_failure_patterns.cause: Automatic semantic-mask or band detection merged glass with masonry/background, or sliced more than one architectural level into a repeatable module.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Store normalized opening_schedule.json and band_schedule.json beside the source. Rasterize exact rectangular, segmental or pointed openings and crop floor, alternate, crown, podium and side bands in both X and Y before PBR derivation. Replace singular chimney, tower or entrance pixels with fixed geometry.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Near-range windows turn into pale or white holes even though the far facade atlas is correct
known_failure_patterns.cause: The recessed pane or occupied room card crosses into a flush solid massing core, so the runtime reveals or transmits the core instead of the authored window assembly.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Inset or thin each structural core to create a continuous facade service cavity. Keep the stone face, return, pane, room card and core in strict depth order and validate the section in the live Google Tiles near LOD.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A requested sibling variant compiles with the geometry or image of the first variant
known_failure_patterns.cause: The export selected the variant description but retained the parent generationStyleInput and variant_0 image provenance.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Derive the selected variant index and rewrite archetypeId, archetypeLabel, archetypeImageUrl and archetypeImagePath before emitting the family source. Assert the exact UI generation id during validation.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A batch reports success but reuses an older GLB after Blender printed a Python traceback
known_failure_patterns.cause: Blender can exit with process code zero after an embedded Python exception, leaving stale output files available to downstream validation.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Treat Blender traceback and compiler error markers in stdout/stderr as hard failures, delete or version output directories per build, and validate manifest provenance against the requested family id.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: An octagonal lantern has detailed cardinal faces but blank diagonal wedges
known_failure_patterns.cause: The massing primitive became eight-sided while facade skins and physical window kits remained limited to front, rear, left and right axes.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Support oriented facade skins and construction-depth window arrays on arbitrary facade angles. Register every exposed polygon face and validate the lantern from aerial plus both diagonal street views.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A ceremonial entrance faces a railway, service lane or interior block instead of the public street
known_failure_patterns.cause: The family front axis was placed with the polygon's stored winding or a default zero rotation rather than an explicit public-frontage edge.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Persist frontage and service-edge semantics in the master-plan payload, derive rotation from the selected street edge, and include a live orientation gate before community acceptance.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Pale stone detail reads well offline but becomes flat white in Google Tiles
known_failure_patterns.cause: Bright runtime exposure, high-value albedo and insufficient mid-frequency normal/AO contrast compress the relief against sunlit photogrammetry.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Calibrate albedo values and PBR contrast in the live viewer, preserve shadow-neutral texture input, and validate the same model under sun-facing, backlit and grazing cameras before changing geometry.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A few hero buildings are convincing but a generated neighborhood is too heavy to orbit or capture as video
known_failure_patterns.cause: The close-range atlas, materials and construction geometry were delivered at one quality tier for every distance and every repeated instance.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Ship explicit hero, district and map LODs; instance shared modules/materials, compress textures with KTX2, preload route-visible assets and enforce district-wide triangle, texture and draw-call budgets.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Windows on a cylindrical turret look like blue decals or unrelated white boxes
known_failure_patterns.cause: The corner tower was fixed geometry but its windows were separate flat front-only curtain walls, so the openings did not follow both exposed tangent planes or the turret's masonry-band language.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Make the two outward tangent elevations part of the fixed turret assembly. Place recessed occupied panes just outside the opaque drum, use construction-depth stone returns, preserve the masonry course rhythm, and validate all four corners from street and aerial obliques.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Semantic graph windows ignore the selected glass profile and remain cool blue while facade-sheet glass is correct
known_failure_patterns.cause: Only masked facade-sheet overlay materials consumed the shared optical profile; generic graph glazing still used the catalogue fallback MAT_Glass values.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Build every unmasked semantic pane from the same profile-driven tint, roughness, transmission, IOR and clearcoat values, keep alpha opaque, and pair it with an always-lit occupied interior card.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A standalone replacement building sits inside a bright white or sky-coloured apron in Google Tiles
known_failure_patterns.cause: The spatial tile mask removes the source photogrammetry across the exact parcel, but an older/manual project has no separate compiled site-boundary surface to cover the cleared ground around an irregular model silhouette.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Mount a deterministic terrain-toned replacement surface under the clipped building footprint, add a small hidden overlap beneath surviving tiles to eliminate raster seams, and treat the entrance threshold and planting edge as the building-to-public-realm handoff.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A model matches the render's facade image but still feels flatter and less architectural than the render
known_failure_patterns.cause: The render carries sectional hierarchy beyond the atlas: deep traceried openings, sculpted arch profiles, roof cresting, projecting belts, steps and a landscaped threshold cast real silhouette and contact shadows.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Compare the live model and approved render at the same close camera. Promote every identity-bearing shadow line into fixed or repeatable construction geometry, then coordinate stairs, retaining edges, planting and furnishings through the public-realm LEGO recipe instead of painting them into the facade.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Windows and carved bays become unnaturally wide when a family is resized to the parcel
known_failure_patterns.cause: One complete facade photograph was UV-stretched across the target span even though it described a shorter authored bay period.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Record the real repeat period and tile only audited ordinary bays. Expand the facade skin, semantic openings, recessed glass and interiors with the identical repeat phase; keep podium, entrance, corners, crown and roof fixed.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A detailed Gothic facade is covered by pale external sticks or a rectangular scaffold
known_failure_patterns.cause: Unreviewed semantic-mask regions were promoted directly into jambs, sills, mullions or returns, and those shapes duplicated construction already visible in the atlas.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Reject broad or merged regions before geometry generation. Use an uncertain mask only for a recessed pane and occupied card; add slim physical returns or sash relief only after an audited opening schedule proves registration from head-on and grazing cameras.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Dark vertical slots remain between a textured wall and fixed cylindrical or polygonal corner towers
known_failure_patterns.cause: The repeatable wall skin stopped short of the corner assembly's inside tangent while the opaque service core remained visible through the gap.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Solve the exposed wall span from the fixed corner geometry. Extend the skin to overlap the inside tangent by a small construction tolerance, keep side spans independent from front spans, and verify every junction in an aerial orbit.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Stone courses, turret bands and eaves look like bright applied graphics in Google Tiles
known_failure_patterns.cause: Relief geometry duplicated atlas bands with excessive projection, thickness or albedo contrast, so it separated visually from the wall material language.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Let the atlas own fine coursing. Use shallow construction-scale relief only for shadow-bearing datums, inherit the same warm stone PBR family, reduce exposed profile, and calibrate in live photogrammetry rather than compensating with brighter materials.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A rounded corner pavilion is a blank drum or contains one impossibly tall facade image
known_failure_patterns.cause: The corner massing was modelled, but floor-accurate facade bands were supported only on cardinal streetwalls and the corner received either no skin or one vertically stretched band.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Compose podium, alternating floor and crown bands on every angled tangent panel at their authored heights. Preserve the curve with several narrow panels and validate seams from street and aerial obliques.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A correctly stepped Art Deco tower still reads as a generic curtain-wall office
known_failure_patterns.cause: Ziggurat massing was correct, but a universal glass grid replaced the reference's punched terra-cotta window rhythm and vertical masonry piers.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Repeat the audited terra-cotta floor band vertically within each fixed shaft tier, align physical piers to the atlas cadence, and keep the podium, setback caps, faceted crown and finial as fixed assemblies.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A variant has plausible geometry but visibly belongs to another sibling archetype
known_failure_patterns.cause: The renderer reused a family-level facade atlas generated from the parent hero image, so a variant-specific material and storey contract was overwritten by an older photographic skin.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Create or resolve an orthographic elevation from the exact selected variant, record audited X/Y band schedules, and bind the facade sheet by variant provenance. Use wall-only crops on repeatable skins; build towers, turrets, roofs and shaped gables as fixed geometry with their own materials.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A timber or mural facade generates huge dark frames and an unexpectedly expensive GLB
known_failure_patterns.cause: Automatic glass segmentation interpreted wood grain, painted motifs, planter shadows or stone joints as thousands of window regions.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Stop before rendering, author normalized openings from the actual sash glass, and regenerate the semantic mask from that schedule. Keep decorative pixels in the albedo only; this removes false construction geometry and restores a bounded triangle budget.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A chalet or heritage building has the correct roof silhouette but still reads as a smooth computer-generated lid
known_failure_patterns.cause: The gable or hip primitive was treated as the finished roof, omitting covering scale, overlapping courses, ballast, ridge and valley metal, gutters and layered verge construction.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Keep the watertight primitive as the base, then add a bounded hero-range surface assembly aligned to each slope. Build repeated tiles or seams as a consolidated mesh; reserve separate low-poly objects for sparse silhouette-bearing weights, cresting or snow retention, and validate from the aerial camera.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A category batch contains convincing materials but several buildings still look like the same rectangular block
known_failure_patterns.cause: The batch inherited a parent massing recipe and changed only facade imagery instead of reconstructing each variant's roof topology, projections, entrances and native proportions.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Cluster variants only for reusable construction kits. Give every exact variant its own fixed graph and use front, oblique and aerial evidence to lock dimensions, ridge axes, cross-gables, balconies, chimneys, glazing halls and roof equipment before rendering the batch.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A clean facade atlas becomes pale panels or a heavy cage in the assembled model
known_failure_patterns.cause: Isolation background entered a rectangular wall crop, or an unregistered physical curtain-wall assembly duplicated the authored glazing and hid the atlas.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Crop to the wall body in both axes, keep gables and roofs out of the band, and add only registered shadow-casting geometry. If a physical pane cannot match the exact authored opening, let the atlas carry it and retain only the reference-proven structural frame.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A roof looks plausible from the street but its ridge direction or solar/valley layout is wrong from above
known_failure_patterns.cause: The graph followed a generic roof label or front-image intuition without checking the 60-degree and 90-degree catalogue views.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Treat aerial evidence as the roof construction drawing. Record the ridge or valley axis explicitly, place cross-gables and equipment in plan coordinates, and require a paired roof-plan comparison board before category release.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A landmark facade looks convincing while the roof court or plan remains wrong
known_failure_patterns.cause: Only the hero camera was measured, and the presentation aerial contained neighbouring context that could not be segmented reliably.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Add a context-free roof_audit camera and a multi-view evidence contract. Score street identity and roof/plan occupancy independently and fail the pilot when either role misses its threshold.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A monumental timber entrance reads as a flat hoop, decal or detached stage prop
known_failure_patterns.cause: The entrance was represented by a two-dimensional arch ring or facade pixels without independent front/back sections, inner reveal or occupied glazing.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use a sampled flared shell with bounded projection, nested laminated layers, construction bevels and a recessed glazed back plane. Validate from head-on, grazing and aerial cameras.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: The assembled asset fails footprint validation even though the building mass is correctly sized
known_failure_patterns.cause: A reference-visible plaza, hexagonal apron or other public-realm surface was joined into the building massing graph.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Remove site context from the exported asset and reconstruct it through the placement/public-realm recipe. Keep only the structural plinth inside the declared footprint.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: The compiled building follows famous real-world metadata but does not resemble the selected catalogue images
known_failure_patterns.cause: Prose for the named real building contradicted the actual UI variant images and silently overruled their massing and material evidence.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Record the conflict and treat the exact selected street, oblique and roof images as the variant contract. Use prose only where it agrees with visible evidence.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Turrets, shaped gables, battlements or roof planes render as large mono-coloured surfaces beside a textured facade
known_failure_patterns.cause: Fixed assemblies referenced colour-only override materials, inherited a sibling roof texture, or reached Blender before the requested texture set was proven available.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Compile material continuity from variant metadata into required material slots and assembly bindings. Fail preflight or runtime when a required landmark lacks a texture key, uses the wrong family, or cannot resolve its texture assets.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A gate or doorway described as deeply recessed is filled by a flat wall or brick panel
known_failure_patterns.cause: The grammar recorded a semantic void, but the target mass remained solid and a rectangular facade skin or portal back plane covered the opening.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Bind the passage to an executable void primitive or Boolean, enforce a reference-derived minimum depth, switch the portal to through-passage mode and split every crossing facade skin around the opening.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A row of arches looks correct head-on but is made from flat decals or only one of the bays is actually recessed
known_failure_patterns.cause: The contract checked for one semantic void and one skin clearance even when the archetype showed a counted arcade or loading-bay run.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Compile the reference-derived opening count into a depth-bearing opening block. Build every pier, head, reveal and back section, and require at least one facade-skin clearance for every opening in the run.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A technically valid building uses the right wall colour but the wrong masonry joints, window shapes or balcony language
known_failure_patterns.cause: A family-level photographic atlas was recoloured and treated as if hue correction made it congruent with the exact selected variant.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use luminance-aware tinting only when construction and opening language already match. If brick must become plaster, sash must become leaded glass, or fixed projections differ, mark the pilot provisional and generate or rectify a variant-native atlas plus audited fixed-detail kit.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A batch reports five successes even though only some models resemble their exact archetype images
known_failure_patterns.cause: Production preflight, runtime material/void gates and GLB validation were conflated with human visual acceptance.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Publish keeper, provisional or rejected status for every model beside a side-by-side exact-reference board. Keep catalogue release blocked until the named human visual-approval contract passes independently.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A model is metadata-correct but its roof, massing or visible material is wrong in the exact archetype comparison
known_failure_patterns.cause: The pipeline ingested a complete metadata description or generic parent prompt instead of admitting only image-confirmed variant facts for bounded purposes.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Declare an image-authoritative evidence policy. Select exact dotted metadata paths one by one with a purpose and image-consistency confirmation, ignore conflicting parent prose, and disable metadata when no field improves the image-derived contract.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A generated building is structurally complete but remains a generic sibling of the exact archetype
known_failure_patterns.cause: Reference images were consulted informally, but their visible storey count, opening schedule, roof axes and material zones were never translated into named graph requirements.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Write an image-lock feature schedule before rendering. Bind every numeric or counted cue to a required node, assembly or void; run production gates; then use side-by-side human review to catch perceptual errors such as an extra storey or incorrect roof value.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: An open market, arcade or entrance looks hollow from one camera but flat or empty from another
known_failure_patterns.cause: The foreground opening has no depth contract, or the void terminates without a recessed occupied surface that establishes a believable interior section.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Pair each real perimeter void with columns or reveals and a deeper occupied backdrop. Wrap the construction around every exposed elevation and verify it from front, corner and rear views rather than accepting a dark facade rectangle.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A validated open market still looks abandoned compared with a richly occupied archetype photograph
known_failure_patterns.cause: The model contains real bays and recessed backdrops but omits the foreground identity layer: counters, crates, produce, task lights and vertical piers that make the public edge legible.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Attach a bounded occupied-stall schedule to the already validated bay positions. Reuse low-cost counters and goods inside each bay, continue structural piers through the header, and keep the through-space and roof topology unchanged.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A heritage entrance has the correct opening size but reads as a black placeholder
known_failure_patterns.cause: One dark slab was used for the entire door opening, omitting leaf panels, fanlight glazing and the small frame relief visible in the archetype.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Split the entrance into a recessed paneled timber leaf and separately framed fanlight. Use real relief and glass at hero range while retaining the image-locked opening dimensions and depth.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A glazed barrel roof reads as coloured plastic or an opaque painted shell
known_failure_patterns.cause: The transmissive surface overlaps an opaque roof, lacks visible supporting structure, or encloses a blank volume that provides nothing credible to transmit or reflect.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Partition opaque and glass roof fields into non-overlapping shells, add silhouette-scale transverse ribs and depth-running purlins, keep the volume below open, and place bounded interior structure or activity where the reference supports it.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A building has the correct overall mass but still looks sparse and cartoonish
known_failure_patterns.cause: The pipeline jumped from large box/roof primitives directly to tiny texture detail, omitting the medium shadow-bearing construction that communicates architectural scale.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Add an explicit medium-detail pass after silhouette approval: bay pilasters, cornice courses, balustrade depth, roof ribs and purlins, edge returns, side-wall openings and fixed landmark furniture. Audit that layer from street, oblique and roof views before adding fine ornament.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Physical glazing is warm and dimensional in Cycles but black or flat in Eevee or the city runtime
known_failure_patterns.cause: The geometry and dielectric material are valid, but the real-time renderer uses a different transmission, environment, reflection or interior-LOD path.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Keep a reproducible Cycles reference, Eevee automation render and exported-GLB runtime capture. Tune renderer-specific optical parity without replacing valid glass with alpha plastic, and record remaining carved or silhouette gaps separately as modeling work.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A high-detail keeper pilot exceeds triangle, material or delivery-envelope budgets
known_failure_patterns.cause: Every rib, ornament and material variation survived as unique geometry or a separate shader after visual approval.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Preserve fixed silhouette and void assemblies, instance or consolidate repeatable members, bake non-silhouette ornament to normal/AO/roughness, merge equivalent materials and downscale only textures whose visual contribution survives side-by-side review.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Stone and roof surfaces look nuanced in Blender but become flat or differently coloured in the exported catalogue model
known_failure_patterns.cause: The look depended on Blender-only procedural, grading or mix nodes that the glTF material path could not reproduce.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Bake the approved surface story into tile-safe albedo, roughness and tangent-space normal images, use metric UV scale, export them through Principled BSDF and require a camera-locked neutral source-versus-reimport parity report.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A less-plastic building still looks like a simplified cartoon of its archetype
known_failure_patterns.cause: Surface variation improved while the clock tower, carved relief, capitals, balustrades or other identity-bearing medium/fine geometry remained generic.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Keep surface QA as a separate passed layer, then return to the exact references and author a bounded fixed ornament kit for the silhouette- and shadow-bearing identity cues. Do not increase grunge or normal strength to compensate for missing construction.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A roof or masonry zone has the right colour but still reads as the wrong material
known_failure_patterns.cause: The surface source came from a broad same-family match, such as wall brick used for pantiles, featureless copper used for standing seam, or sandstone recoloured as brownstone.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Assign an explicit construction role to each baked material, select a source with the matching joint, course, seam or overlap pattern, and compare it against the exact aerial or facade evidence before accepting the bake.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A neutral source-versus-GLB audit reports high similarity despite an obvious facade colour or texture shift
known_failure_patterns.cause: Whole-frame error was dominated by a shared studio background and ground plane, allowing a small building foreground to contribute too little to the score.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Render both neutral views over transparency and compute colour error plus silhouette overlap only on the union of their alpha-masked building pixels. Keep the full-building foreground mean error at or below five percent.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A baked roof stays dark even though the profile declares a pale roof base colour
known_failure_patterns.cause: The exported Principled material receives its visible colour from a dark baked albedo image, so the declaration cannot recolour the delivered pixels.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Derive and audit a construction-role-correct pale albedo bake, bind that texture key to the roof slot and rerun both the exact-aerial comparison and GLB surface-finish audit.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Loggias or window bays appear as floating cages in front of an otherwise correct facade
known_failure_patterns.cause: The same feature was encoded once in the rectified facade/glazing sheet and again as a complete projecting frame or balcony assembly.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Choose one owner for the feature, remove the redundant assembly and retain physical geometry only for depth, silhouettes or rails that the facade sheet cannot credibly supply.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A catalogue batch renders successfully but contains targets that never received exact-variant architectural authoring or visual approval
known_failure_patterns.cause: The catalogue was treated as an unattended rendering queue, so inherited parent profiles and generic sheets were mistaken for production readiness.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Partition the catalogue into representative and sibling phases, require exact-profile and audited-sheet readiness before rendering, limit batches to five, and stop at a human exact-reference checkpoint after each batch.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Concrete has the right pale colour but reads as square precast cladding instead of board-formed construction
known_failure_patterns.cause: A broad concrete-family source was relabelled without changing its visible joint hierarchy.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Bind the material to a board-formed construction role, bake horizontal shutter-board courses with restrained staggered joints and inspect the result in the exact facade comparison before release.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A polished exact-variant facade contains arched windows where the reference has rectangular openings, or repeats the wrong number of storeys
known_failure_patterns.cause: The image model treated architectural identity as a soft style prompt and was not checked against a counted opening and storey schedule before the atlas entered Blender.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Record opening shape and storey count as hard visual-review fields. Reject and regenerate semantically wrong atlases; do not try to hide the error with massing, tinting or stronger surface detail.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A modern curtain-wall building resembles a cage and consumes excessive geometry
known_failure_patterns.cause: The compiler created deep returns and frames for every detected window even though the registered atlas and fixed structural grid already owned the repeated facade system.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use a mask-only physical glass overlay for large repeated modern elevations, retain only silhouette- and shadow-bearing structural members, and reserve full return assemblies for identity-bearing openings.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A ten-building checkpoint contains several attractive models but the campaign is nevertheless unsafe to expand to one hundred
known_failure_patterns.cause: Machine validation and a few keeper examples were treated as evidence that the methodology generalizes across semantic opening, proportion, roof and export cases.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Publish a per-building keeper/provisional/rejected table beside the four-view comparison board. Repair or explicitly defer every rejected case before authorizing the next finite batch.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A Blender source render is faithful but the re-imported GLB loses facade detail or develops halos around semantic panels
known_failure_patterns.cause: Alpha-bearing image maps were transcoded through a lossy export format, changing edge coverage and colour even though the material and geometry were unchanged.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Keep alpha-bearing semantic textures lossless, export with automatic PNG preservation, and reject the asset unless the alpha-masked neutral source-versus-GLB foreground comparison passes.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A machine-valid model still has the wrong overall architectural character
known_failure_patterns.cause: Automated topology, material and parity gates were allowed to stand in for a per-building exact-reference architectural judgement.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Require a named architect to inspect the mandatory six-view board, score that individual building at least 85/100 and record every hard-stop proportion, roof, void, material-continuity or side/rear error before release.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A deep arcade still looks like a generic barrel, Gothic ogive, mushroom or second arch placed inside the decorative portal
known_failure_patterns.cause: The sticker clearance and tunnel section were generated from an assumed style formula or a trace of the surrounding ornament instead of the exact inner negative opening contour. The lining then became a dominant foreground shape even though the passage had real depth.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Extract and version the binary inner-opening contour from the registered source, validate its centre, neck, shoulder, crown and scale anchors, use that identical contour for sticker clearance and section extrusion, and inset it so only a narrow reveal is visible. Keep the building rejected until six-view architect review clears 85/100.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A highly accurate continuous facade sticker develops opaque, doubled or misaligned windows after physical glazing is added
known_failure_patterns.cause: A generic pane schedule was placed over photographed openings without an opening-accurate semantic mask in the sticker's canonical registration frame.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Keep the sticker as the visible owner of glazing and frames until an exact registered glass mask exists. Permit physical optical depth only within that mask, preserve separate silhouette and reveal geometry, and reject any overlay whose opening count, centres, floor datums or boundaries drift from the image lock.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A beautiful front sticker is attached to a generic roof box with blank side and rear elevations
known_failure_patterns.cause: Sticker generation began before a source-matched whole-building silhouette, roof proxy and elevation-occupancy contract had passed, so the detailed front concealed incomplete architectural massing until final review.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Gate sticker generation behind an approved clay roof/silhouette proxy and all-elevation opening map derived from street, oblique and aerial evidence. Reject doubled gables, blank visible elevations and unregistered overlays before paid image generation; camera-match the final architect board independently from export-parity tests.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A whole-building sticker pilot shows white borders, flat roof colour or an entrance volume projecting in front of its photographed opening
known_failure_patterns.cause: The image isolation background was registered as part of the wall, the roof sticker replaced the complete PBR material instead of only its albedo, or the depth-bearing opening block was centred without aligning its outer face to the facade plane.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Preserve the generated master, derive a render-ready edge-to-edge occupied crop, register roof imagery in one declared plan frame while retaining construction-role normal and roughness, and calculate opening-block centre from facade plane plus half depth. Compare front, rear-corner and roof-audit views before release.
